title: What Is Salvation?
subtitle: A path of faith, repentance, and mercy before the one God
summary: Islam offers salvation as a way back to the Creator: worship Him alone, turn from wrongdoing, live faithfully, and trust His mercy. Each person answers for their own acts, but forgiveness is not a wage. Accepting this path also calls for reasons to trust the Quran and Muhammad as bearers of God's guidance.

seo.metaTitle: What Is Salvation? Islam and Christianity Compared
seo.metaDescription: Why Islam joins faith, repentance, righteous action, and God's mercy—and how that differs from salvation through Christ.

sections.title: A Way Back to God
sections.body:
Salvation in Islam is not escape from duty. It means being saved from sin and its final consequences by returning to the one God. The wrongdoer still answers for the wrong; God, who knows the person fully, can forgive.

This gives a reason to take Islam seriously. It joins a duty to face wrongdoing with an open path to mercy. No one needs to inherit another person's guilt or worship a messenger to return to God.

sections.title: What Does a Sinner Need?
sections.body:
A serious account of salvation must explain more than how to avoid punishment. It must say what is wrong, why forgiveness is possible, and how a renewed relationship with God changes a life.

Islam begins with the Creator, not a person's religious ancestry. Faith turns toward Him, repentance faces the wrong, and good action puts that return into practice. Mercy is not a reward that someone can demand for finishing a religious checklist.

sections.title: Why Responsibility and Mercy Belong Together
sections.body:
Being guilty is not the same as being beyond repair. Unrelated good deeds cannot make a betrayal harmless. Yet admitting the wrong and changing course need not be pointless just because the past cannot be undone.

Quran 6:164 keeps the burden with the person who acts. Quran 39:53 gives hope of forgiveness even to those who have gravely wronged themselves. Together, these passages call for a serious return—not excuses for the wrong and not lasting despair.

sections.title: The Christian Alternative Deserves a Fair Hearing
sections.body:
Historic Christianity centers salvation on Christ's death and resurrection. But Christians do not all explain grace, faith, and works in the same way. The [Catholic Catechism](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_three/section_one/chapter_three/article_2/ii_grace.html) emphasizes grace that enables a free response. [Orthodox teaching](https://www.oca.org/orthodoxy/the-orthodox-faith/doctrine-scripture/the-symbol-of-faith/redemption) includes healing the relationship with God and victory over death. The [Reformed Protestant Westminster Confession, chapter 11](https://opc.org/wcf.html) centers justification—being accepted as righteous before God—through faith in Christ.

None of these teaches that people can buy God's favor. The dispute with Islam concerns who Christ is and how he saves, not whether Christians value mercy or a changed life.

sections.title: The Quran's Pattern of Return
sections.body:
Quran 2:25 and 103:1–3 connect faith with good action. The latter also includes truth and patient endurance in a life of faith. Salvation is thus not just a private claim to believe, with no effect on conduct.

Quran 2:62 also connects reward with faith in God, the Last Day, and righteousness. It calls for a real response to God, not just birth into a community. Its scope is read within the Quran's wider teaching on revelation. It does not guarantee salvation through a religious label alone.

sections.title: What the New Testament Adds
sections.body:
Ephesians 2:8–9 rules out boasting in human achievement. James 2:17 challenges faith without action. Matthew 7:21 warns against calling oneself loyal without doing the Father's will. Romans 10:9 connects salvation with confessing Jesus as Lord and believing in his resurrection.

The shared concern for conduct is real, and so is the difference. The New Testament centers salvation on Christ; it cannot simply be relabeled Islam. Islam does not make Christ's saving work the condition of God's mercy.

sections.title: An Objection: What if God Saves Through Christ?
sections.body:
A Christian can fairly object that God's ability to forgive directly does not prove this is the way He chose. Christians understand the cross as God's own saving act, not an unrelated victim forcing a merciless God to become kind. That reply blocks an easy but weak argument against Christianity.

Islam's response has two parts. First, holding people to account while accepting their repentance makes sense of forgiveness. The fact that people sin does not, by itself, prove a need for divine sacrifice. Second, claims about the way God chose must be tested against the evidence for revelation. [Forgiveness in Islam and Christianity](/articles/forgiveness-in-islam-and-christianity) examines this dispute more fully.

sections.title: Mercy Does Not Make Conduct Optional
sections.body:
The Prophet's teaching in [Sahih al-Bukhari 5673](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5673) denies that anyone's deeds alone secure Paradise—even his own. The same report urges good, steady action and gives a wrongdoer room to repent.

Mercy thus has a daily role. The believer acts without claiming to have put God in debt, then returns after failure without treating it as permission to keep sinning. Harm to others still needs repair.

sections.title: Why This Path Deserves a Hearing
sections.body:
Islam's appeal is not simply that it has fewer steps. Worship stays with the Creator, blame follows actual wrongdoing, and hope rests on God's mercy rather than ancestry or a claim to be perfect.

These features give reasons to examine it. They do not, on their own, prove that Muhammad is a prophet. [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) and [Who Is Prophet Muhammad?](/articles/who-is-prophet-muhammad) take up the evidence for that further belief.

sections.title: From Belief to a Changed Life
sections.body:
Salvation becomes a practical question when it meets a wrong that needs to stop or a right that needs to be restored. [Sin and Repentance](/articles/sin-and-repentance) explains that return in more detail.

Islam invites a life before God: sincere worship, honest repentance, steady good action, and trust in mercy. It asks for neither denial of guilt nor despair over it.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Can good deeds purchase Paradise in Islam?
A: No. Sahih al-Bukhari 5673 makes God's mercy essential. Good deeds are still required and matter, but they do not put God in debt or force Him to grant eternal life.

Q: Does Christianity teach that behavior is irrelevant?
A: No. Christians differ over how works relate to being made right with God and being saved. Ephesians 2:8–9, James 2:17, and Matthew 7:21 need to be read together, not reduced to that slogan.

Q: Does a coherent account of salvation prove Islam true?
A: Not by itself. An account that fits together gives a reason to listen. Accepting it as God's guidance also calls for evidence about the Quran and Muhammad's claim to be a prophet.

Q: Does Quran 2:62 make a religious label sufficient?
A: No. The verse names faith in God, the Last Day, and good action. Its scope must be read within the Quran as a whole; birth into a religious group is not a blank guarantee.

sections.title: Sources and Further Study
sections.body:
The Quran and Bible passages appear in the scripture cards. The linked Catholic, Orthodox, and Reformed sources state their own positions; they are not interchangeable.

[Grace, Mercy, Faith, and Deeds](/articles/grace-mercy-faith-deeds) examines why effort matters without buying Paradise. The books below offer broader theological context.

quranVerses.arabic: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۖ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا۟ مِنْهَا مِن ثَمَرَةٍۢ رِّزْقًۭا ۙ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ ۖ وَأُتُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُتَشَٰبِهًۭا ۖ وَلَهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَٰجٌۭ مُّطَهَّرَةٌۭ ۖ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before." And it is given to them in likeness. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
quranVerses.translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans [before Prophet Muhammad] - those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.

quranVerses.arabic: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
quranVerses.translation: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ قُلْ يَٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quranVerses.translation: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِى رَبًّۭا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ ۚ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quranVerses.translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ."
